Subject: Request: admin activity evidence for SOC 2 audit — timeframe & export options

Hi Avery,

We're starting SOC 2 evidence collection for our auditor and need a clear statement of what Redwood logs for admin/operator activity, how long those records are retained, and what export options you support. Specifically our auditor asked for:

- A list of admin event types captured (console, API, role changes, privilege elevations, key rotations, etc.)
- Timestamp fidelity and timezone handling
- Default retention windows and extended-retention options for enterprise customers
- Export formats and delivery methods (signed manifests, checksums, SFTP/presigned, streaming)
- Any PII redaction/hashing options during export

Can you provide a delivery plan and whether you can provide a one-time snapshot plus daily delta exports for the last 12 months?

Subject: Re: Request: admin activity evidence for SOC 2 audit — clocked export procedure and retention

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear checklist. Below is a condensed playbook we can use to satisfy your auditor. I'm copying Marissa (compliance lead) and Ben (infra/exports) to handle manifesting and delivery.

Summary (short):
- What we log: administrative console actions (create/delete/update), API key lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke), role and group changes, privilege elevations (grant/revoke of admin scopes), console & API authentication (success/fail), session starts/stops and IP, deployment events for model-serving configs, operator-initiated data access requests, and policy changes (IAM, network).
- Retention: default admin-event ledger retention = 18 months. Enterprise customers can purchase extended retention up to 5 years (contracted).
- Timestamping: events are recorded with RFC3339 timestamps normalized to UTC, and we preserve the original client/local timezone string when available. We also include monotonic sequence ids for ordering (helps with clock skew).
- Export options:
  * Clocked snapshot: full daily snapshot at 00:00:00 UTC boundary ("clocked export") — consistent snapshot boundaries for auditor timelines.
  * Delta exports: incremental nightly deltas (new events since last snapshot) in newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) or CSV.
  * Delivery: presigned S3 URLs (temporary), SFTP push, or secure HTTPS pull with mutual TLS. Each export is accompanied by a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums per file, GPG signature optional).
  * For very large exports we support chunked archives (gzip+tar) with per-chunk checksums and a top-level manifest.
- PII handling: exports can be delivered in three modes: raw (no redaction), hashed (SHA256 with per-tenant salt — irreversible), or redacted (fields removed). We recommend hashed identifiers for auditor use unless they require raw values.

Operational notes:
- We can produce a one-time full snapshot going back 12 months (where data exists) plus nightly deltas going forward. Full snapshot throughput dependent on retention period size; estimate for Medicon (approx 120M events/year) — full export ~420GB compressed, will take ~18 hours to prepare.
- SLA for on-demand snapshots: standard turnaround 7 business days; expedited (48–72 hours) available with expedited fee.
- For chain-of-custody we provide: signed manifest, file-level checksums, export timestamps, operator who requested the export, and delivery audit log (SFTP session logs or presigned URL issuance info).

Attachments included: sample admin-event CSV (admin-event-sample-202702.csv) and a signed-manifest example (signed-manifest-example-202702.txt).

Next steps:
1) Confirm desired PII mode (raw / hashed / redacted) and preferred delivery method.
2) Confirm export window (we'll assume 2026-02-01 to 2027-02-01 for the 12-month snapshot unless you request otherwise).
3) If you need timezone-normalized logs with original tz strings preserved, confirm and we'll include both UTC and original offset fields.

Marissa/Ben — please pick this up for sizing & manifesting once Jessica confirms the mode + delivery.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Security Liaison

Avery / Ben — quick follow-up on timestamp and manifest details from an auditor perspective:

- Timestamps: auditors like to see both event_timestamp_utc and event_timestamp_local (with offset) plus a monotonic_event_id. We will include event ingestion timestamp and event source if available.
- Timezone normalization: we'll standardize exports to UTC for the "clocked snapshot" boundary, and include local tz in a separate column to show original context.
- Manifest: top-level manifest will be JSONL (one entry per payload file) with fields: filename, sha256, byte_count, export_window_start, export_window_end, produced_by, gpg_signature (if requested). Example line included below.

Example manifest line (human-readable):
# {filename: admin-events-20270201-20270228.ndjson, sha256: <hex>, bytes: 23452345, start: 2027-02-01T00:00:00Z, end: 2027-02-28T23:59:59Z, produced_by: exports@redwood.com}

Ben — please include estimated S3 presigned expiry default (we usually do 7 days) and whether we can provide ephemeral SFTP creds for the auditor team. If Medicon wants GPG signing we need their public key; otherwise we'll sign with our export-service key and include full chain.

Marissa Cole
Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
